open_points.subject: StaffAccount email-verified mark
open_points.text: A staff account keeps a recorded "email verified" mark: the administrator's activation, the first administrator's creation (R0-07) and the recovery override (R0-20) set it
open_points.question: What value does the mark have when an administrator creates a pending staff account, and can any event clear or otherwise change it after it is set?
options: The mark starts false and becomes permanently true on activation
The mark is already true at account creation
The mark may be null or derived until one of the named events sets it
open_points.default_guess: Store false on ordinary account creation, set true atomically with activation, and never clear it.

witness.initial: An administrator is authorized to create staff accounts, and no account exists for new.operator@example.com.
events: The administrator creates the account; it remains pending_verification.
An authorized caller reads the account before activation.
outcomes: The returned email-verified mark is false.
The returned mark is true or absent because its initial state was not specified.
witness.observer: The caller reading the pending staff account

open_points.subject: Staff account view exposing the email-verified mark
open_points.question: Which concrete operation returns this mark, and which principal types or capabilities are allowed to observe it?
options: Only an administrator-facing staff-account detail operation
The account holder's own account/profile operation
Both administrator and self-service account views
open_points.default_guess: Return it from the administrator-authorized staff-account detail operation only.

witness.initial: An active operator account has its email-verified mark set.
events: The operator requests whatever self/account information the implementation provides.
An administrator requests that operator's staff-account details.
outcomes: Only the administrator's response contains the mark.
Both the operator's self response and the administrator's response contain the mark.
witness.observer: The operator and administrator API clients

open_points.subject: Lost-password replacement account
open_points.text: an administrator may disable that account and create a new one
open_points.question: How can the replacement account be created when the disabled account still owns the mandatory unique normalized login email?
options: The replacement must use a different email
The administrator must first use the recovery override to move the old account to another email
Disabling an account releases its email for reuse
A dedicated atomic replacement operation transfers the email
open_points.default_guess: Require the administrator to move the disabled account to another unique email through the audited recovery override, then create the new account with the original email.

witness.initial: An operator account for worker@example.com is active, the holder has lost the password, and the administrator wants the replacement to retain worker@example.com as its login.
events: The administrator disables the old account.
The administrator attempts to create the promised new account using worker@example.com.
outcomes: Creation fails because normalized email uniqueness still includes disabled accounts.
Creation succeeds because disabling releases the email or the implementation silently treats this as replacement.

open_points.subject: Sole-administrator host-level recovery
open_points.text: such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product
open_points.question: Who is trusted to perform this recovery, what concrete host-level action and inputs recover the administrator, what state may it change, and what observable success and failure outcomes does it have?
options: A local command resets the existing administrator's password
A local command replaces the existing administrator's login email and password
A host operator directly repairs persistent state under an operational procedure
open_points.default_guess: Provide a local, interactive host command that identifies the sole administrator, replaces its password hash, preserves its identity and assignments, and returns closed success/refusal exit codes without printing secrets.

witness.initial: The deployment has exactly one active administrator, who no longer knows either the login email or password; R0-07 bootstrap refuses because a staff account exists.
events: The host operator invokes the unspecified host-level recovery.
The administrator attempts to sign in using the recovery result.
outcomes: The existing administrator receives a new password while retaining identity, assignments, and email.
The recovery changes the login email, creates or enables another administrator, or requires direct database repair, producing different identity and audit consequences.
witness.observer: The host operator and the recovered administrator
